newsitem.title: USA: Ryder CEO sees auto-carrier arm selling soon.
newsitem.headline: Ryder CEO sees auto-carrier arm selling soon.

text.p: Ryder System Inc chief executive Anthony Burns said on Monday the company was actively talking to possible buyers of its automotive-carrier unit and would probably announce a sale soon.

Burns said in a telephone conference call that Ryder expected to get more than book value and all cash for the transporter of trucks and cars. He gave no figures on the value of the unit, which last year had revenues of $583.3 million.
"We expect to announce a resolution soon," Burns said.

Burns said the company had not decided what use it would make of the money realized from the sale but said Ryder's management and board of directors believed strongly in share buybacks when the company had excess capital.

Ryder last fall sold its consumer truck-rental unit as part of a campaign to improve financial performance and just completed a large share buyback. The company has also cut staff and transferred some operations such as computer services to outside companies.

Ryder's Automotive Carrier Services unit transported more than six million vehicles in North America last year but reported a full-year pre-tax loss of $14.7 million and a two percent decline in revenues. The company said the 1996 loss was due to restructuring charges, higher fuel costs and higher wages in a new contract with the Teamsters union.
The unit was profitable during the first three months of 1997, Ryder said in its quarterly earnings report released earlier Monday.
